audit.whatIsWrong: Sanguine Pool is the tracked, matchup-defining ability in every string of the full layer and the pivot of the entire content layer, and its cooldown is never given once — the closest the entry gets is 'watch its long early cooldown'.
audit.why: It is 28 seconds at rank 1, falling to 16 at rank 5, and it costs him no resource. Twenty-eight seconds is the largest single window Ambessa gets in this lane and it is the difference between 'bait the pool' as a slogan and as a plan: spend the pool, then you have half a minute in which a 1250-range blink-suppress has no answer. The duration matters too — 2 seconds untargetable is long enough to eat the suppress AND the slam, which is why ulting on a live pool loses the whole 130s ultimate for nothing.
audit.corrected: Sanguine Pool (W), 28/25/22/19/16, no cost: 2 seconds untargetable. Bait it, then all-in inside the 28s.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json — W Sanguine Pool 'becoming untargetable for 2 seconds', cd 28/25/22/19/16, cost 0

audit.whatIsWrong: Tides of Blood is named four times as poke, but neither of its two exploitable properties appears anywhere: it costs Vladimir his own health, and enemy units block it.
audit.why: Both change how the lane is played and both favour Ambessa. Because minions block the charged release, standing behind your own caster wave converts his main poke tool into nothing — a melee champion can choose that position and a ranged one usually cannot. And because it is paid for in health, a poke war he 'wins' still walks him down toward the health bar where your combo kills him. The entry instead frames his poke as free chip that Ambessa simply has to absorb until level 6.
audit.corrected: Tides of Blood (E), 13/11/9/7/5, no mana: he pays his own health to charge it, and enemy units block the release. Stand behind your casters.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json — E Tides of Blood: 'Vladimir pays his own health to charge up a reservoir of blood which, when released, deals damage in the area around him but can be blocked by enemy units', cd 13/11/9/7/5

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings credit Ambessa with 'your R's armor-pen passive and ability-damage healing' / 'your R's armor pen and ability-damage healing' / 'your armor-pen passive' (spikes[2].text, whys[5], late). One string calls her empowered attack a 'Medarda-empowered auto' (spikes[0].text).
audit.why: Public Execution grants no armour penetration and no healing in Riot's text — it is a 1250-range blink to the farthest champion in a chosen line, a suppress, then a slam for damage and a stun. The kit file's 'heal' flag on R is a tooltip-parsing misfire (see notes). 'Medarda-empowered auto' is not an ability name either; the empowered attack comes from Drakehound's Step (P), which is what a player has to look for on the ability bar. Both mistakes make the same page unusable in the same way — they describe buttons and stats that are not there.
audit.corrected: Drakehound's Step (P) empowers the next attack with bonus range, damage and attack speed. Public Execution (R), 1250 range, 130/115/100 — blink, suppress, slam. No armour pen, no heal.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json — P Drakehound's Step, R Public Execution

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization says 'Anti-heal early — his healing fights your pattern' and 'boots Mercury's Treads', but Crimson Pact is never mentioned and Hemoplague's healing is never mentioned.
audit.why: Crimson Pact converts every 30 bonus health into 1 AP and every 1 AP into 1.6 bonus health, so the usual bruiser answer of stacking health against a mage is partly self-defeating information for the player reading this page: Vladimir is the champion whose damage grows with the health HE buys, and the durability race is one Ambessa cannot enter. Hemoplague is 120s flat and heals him for each champion hit, which is the exact moment Grievous Wounds has to already be applied rather than bought.
audit.corrected: Crimson Pact turns his bonus health into AP and back — burst plus Grievous Wounds beats it. Hemoplague is 120s flat and heals him per champion hit, so the anti-heal must be on before he casts.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json — P Crimson Pact, R Hemoplague cd 120 with heal flag

audit.why: EVEN at 6/10 with Vladimir carry threat 8.5/10 is the right shape: Ambessa owns levels 2-3 against a champion with a famously weak early game, gets one clean window at 6, and loses the scaling race. Difficulty and carry numbers unchanged.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart contradicts its own text at the two late stages. win[5] and phases[5].side say Ambessa wins First item while whys[5] and spikes[2].text both say 'Vlad turns the corner here'; win[6] and phases[6].side say Ambessa wins 2+ items while whys[6] and spikes[3].text say 'he reclaims the lane and out-scales you'.
audit.why: This is the same tail-end inversion the vayne entry has, which suggests a generator bug rather than seven independent judgement calls. I did not flip it — chart edits are atomic and mirrored, and inventing a power shift is worse than a visible inconsistency — but the prose is the half that matches the kit: Crimson Pact scaling and a 4.6-second Transfusion at rank 5 are Vladimir's game, not Ambessa's.
audit.corrected: Kit maths put Vladimir ahead at First item and at 2+ items. Needs a human decision before the chart is touched — see questionsForUser.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your soft spot: your cooldowns are longest here while his Tides of Blood (E) poke and Transfusion (Q) heal chip you as you wait on 6. Don't trade into a Vlad sitting on a full Sanguine Pool. At 6 everything flips for one window — Public Execution blinks you behind him and suppresses, so bait the pool first (or watch its long early cooldown) and ult the instant it's down. If he pools mid-cast he goes untargetable and your suppress whiffs, so the whole kill is a pool-timing read — but past first item the lane starts tilting back to him as his AP and sustain scale.

This bogus flag has now surfaced as invented 'R armor-pen / on-ability healing' text in the urgot, vayne and vladimir entries — treat it as a file-wide sweep. UNVERIFIED, NOT ASSERTED: whether Sanguine Pool's untargetability can break an already-applied Public Execution suppression, as opposed to dodging the cast. The existing text says he can pool 'mid-cast' and I left those strings alone rather than sharpen a timing claim the kits cannot settle.
